she/her pronouns, and I am a Senior Policy Advocate at Maine Equal Justice, a nonprofit
civil legal aid provider working to increase economic security, opportunity, and equity for
people in Maine. As a member of the Blue Ribbon Commission to Design a Plan for
Sustained Investment in Preventing Disease and improving the Health of Maine
Communities, I am testifying in support of both LD 1658 and LD1772, as amended.

The Fund for a Healthy Maine (FHM) was created to receive Maine's tobacco settlement payments and allocate those payments to support the treatment and prevention of chronic disease and the promotion of individual and population level health. However, due to the decline in tobacco settlement payments, which are based on national sales of combustion
cigarettes (vapes, nicotine pouches, and cannabis are not included), the FHM and the
programs it supports face a financial deficit if Maine lawmakers do not act.

Both LD 1658 and LD 1772 create pathways toward financial solvency and the long-term sustainability ofthe FHM. In keeping with the recommendations put forth by the 2024 Blue Ribbon Commission, LD1658 would create an annual transfer of a percentage ofthe tobacco excise tax revenue from the General Fund to the FHM. This not only addresses the fund's financial shortfall, but it would also add an important element of equity. People with low income pay the price of commercial tobacco twice--first when they are targeted by the tobacco industry through predatory marketing and advertising in low-income communities and second when they lose a higher percentage of their limited incomes to tobacco taxes.`

LD 1658, An Act to Preserve and Strengthen the Fund for a Healthy Maine
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services

Good afternoon, Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and honorable members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services. As you know, I am Representative Anne
Graham and I am proud to represent the towns of North Yarmouth and the majority of Gray in
the Maine House. I thank you for allowing me to present an amended version of LD 1658, An
Act to Preserve and Strengthen the Fund for a Healthy Maine.

The Fund for a Healthy Maine (FHM) is an incredible success story and reflects the best qualities
of Maine people. It has an imovative, intercomected and youth-focused design; responsible alignment with the purpose of the tobacco settlement; prudent recognition that prevention is always the best medicine; and 25 years of loyal and unyielding support from policymakers, stakeholder groups and Maine people.
As this committee has been aware, the FHM has been approaching a financial crossroads for
several years, caused by declining tobacco settlement payments (which are based on national cigarette sales and do not include the sales of vaping products and nicotine pouches in payment calculations). While this looming structural deficit has been masked by the availability of unspent funds, those carryover funds will be exhausted in fiscal year 2027.
The Maine Legislature stepped up to protect the FHM in the continuing services budget that
passed in March 2025. That action in such a challenging environment was much appreciated by Maine's public health professionals and acknowledged the value of prevention for Maine people and communities. But that was a one-time solution for an ongoing problem, so the future of the
Fund remains uncertain.

We are now in a moment of opportunity. We can take one final step to assure the Fund for a
Healthy Maine, and its critical public health and prevention programs, are financially stable and
secure for years to come -- rather than leaving Maine's long-standing prevention and public
health investments vulnerable to capsize in variable political winds. LD 1658 offers a route
forward.

District l05: North Yarrnouth and Gray

LD 1658 creates an ongoing transfer of a portion of tobacco excise tax revenue from the General
Fund to the Fund for a Healthy Maine so this special revenue account has the resources needed each year to maintain its baseline investments in public health and prevention. This straightforward solution aligns and integrates Maine's use of tobacco excise tax revenue in the General Fund with our tobacco settlement revenue in the Fund for a Healthy Maine. This is particularly appropriate as both are intended to prevent tobacco use and illness and support the health and well-being of Maine people across generations. Maine experts and policymakers agree. Maine's 2024 Blue Ribbon Commission recommended
this solution for the approaching FHM structural deficit with unanimous and bipartisan support
from all participating legislators. And in March 2025, our committee's report back on LD 210
from the 132"" Legislature unanimously recommended directing a portion of General Fund revenue from tobacco taxes as the means to resolving the shortfall in the Fund for a Healthy Maine. Thank you for that support. The foundational value and necessity of prevention and public health do not change with politicians and administrations. Rather, these are constants that must be met with stable and secure funding for well-planned investments that meet the needs and circumstances of people and communities. Creating an annual and ongoing transfer of tobacco excise tax revenue into the
FHM will secure Maine's investment in prevention and position us to be strong and responsive
to future health concerns.
Maine can be proud of our Fund for a Healthy Maine legacy. We have consistently used the Fund to support the health of Maine people. We can and must protect Maine's only dedicated source of ftmding for prevention by securing the FHM for future generations. Thank you for your support in the past. I urge you to unanimously support LD 1658.

Good afternoon. Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and Distinguished Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services. My name is Art Blank, and I am a Board Member of Healthy Acadia, which provides public health services primarily across Hancock and Washington counties. I live in Hancock County, and I am testifying in support of LD 1772 and LD 1658.
LD 1772 creates an independent, non-partisan body of public health experts (the Maine Commission on Public Health and Prevention) who will be available to legislators as a timely resource in crisis situations, or otherwise. It will help legislators ground public health decisions with timely access to public health expertise.
The bill proposes solutions for some current state government inefficiencies and plans ahead for a stronger, healthier Maine supported by better, more cost-effective public health infrastructure. Part of the Commission's mission would be to support the Maine CDC in their mandate to create and implement a comprehensive state health plan (it hasn't been fully implemented because of lack of funding to meet existing mandates). This would help build efficiencies in state public health functioning by creating a platform to integrate the state health planning process in cross-referencing other departmental public health plans and initiatives.
A key part of this proposal is the creation of a Fund for A Healthy Maine (FHM) Stabilization Account. That account will provide funding for the creation and functioning of the Commission, in part by leveraging tobacco excise tax dollars, as described in the paragraph below on LD 1658.
If implemented in this way, the FHM Stabilization Account will eliminate the existing need for a loan from the General Fund to fund programming supported by the FHM, which will create efficiencies in the state budget. And it provides a critically-needed way to continue to fund future public health investments via a balanced FHM budget.
Maine people are resourceful, determined, innovative, independent and community-minded and the FHM reflects this, with 25 years of ongoing support - such as the protections for FHM and its programs in the current budget, for which we want to thank our legislators. But in the big picture, the FHM is threatened. The tobacco industry is finding ways around the tobacco master settlement agreement and new ways to appeal to young people and to create lifelong tobacco customers.
LD 1658 proposes to fund FHM programming via a portion of the newly revised tobacco excise tax. With new products, new advertising, and a new generation of tobacco users, tobacco use remains the leading preventable cause of disease, death, and disability in the US. Using tobacco excise tax dollars to support tobacco use prevention and other

preventative health programming in the FHM is exactly why the FHM was created. The strategies funded by the FHM are key to preventing young people from starting to use tobacco, and in preventing healthcare costs associated with tobacco-related illness.
Please vote in support of LD 1772 and LD 1658. On multiple fronts, these bills will help us to collectively build a better Maine.
Sincerely, Art Blank

Testimony of Carol Kelly, Pivot Point Inc. January 7, 2026
Senator lngwersen, Representative Meyer, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and
Human Services. My name is Carol Kelly and lam a public health planning and policy consultant in Portland. l am here today in strong support of LD 1658, An Act To Preserve and Strengthen the Fund for a Healthy
Maine.
My first job in public health was in the early days of the tobacco settlement and the creation ofthe Fund
for a Healthy Maine (FHM). The Fund is an inspiring example of collaborative and responsible policymaking that has been making a real difference in the health of Maine youth and in the vibrancy of our communities.
Thank you for all you do, every year, to protect and defend this special source of funding -- Maine's primary source of funding ~ for prevention and public health.
While the mission ofthe Fund is highly-valued, the financial health of the Fund has been destabilized by declining tobacco settlement payments. The structural deficit in the Fund that has been looming for several
years is now unavoidable.
The budget this Legislature passed last year for fiscal years 2026 and 2027 addressed the Fund's structural shortfall with a one-time transfer from the General Fund. This followed a unanimous recommendation from this committee to use a portion of tobacco excise tax revenue to assure the Fund for a Healthy Maine
could continue its baseline operations in what is now the current biennium.
it would be difficult to articulate how much the public health community appreciated what you did, in such an uncertain environment, to make sure the important prevention and public health initiatives funded by
the Fund for a Healthy Maine could continue. But the root problem is not yet solved.
LD 1658 looks ahead to fiscal year 2028 and beyond and proposes a simple and ongoing solution to the Fund's structural deficit. LD 1658 mirrors this committee's recommendation by proposing a specific percentage of tobacco excise tax revenue be credited each year to the FHM.
Using tobacco excise tax revenue to create a third revenue stream flowing annually into the Fund for a Healthy Maine is a particularly appropriate alignment of funding sources and uses, as both the tobacco settlement and the tobacco excise tax are intended to prevent chronic illness and support good health and

LD 1658 creates an annual and ongoing transfer of a portion of tobacco excise tax revenue into the Fund for a Healthy Maine. Colleen Brown Whiting LD 1658
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services:
I am submitting this testimony to express serious concern regarding the sponsor amendment to L.D. 1658, which removes proposed tobacco tax increases but replaces them with a statutory mandate guaranteeing no less than $65 million annually for the Fund for a Healthy Maine, along with a permanent and increasing diversion of tobacco tax revenue to that fund.
I want to be clear at the outset: I support public health initiatives and prevention efforts. The Fund for a Healthy Maine has historically supported tobacco prevention, chronic disease prevention, health promotion, and community-based programs intended to improve long-term outcomes for Maine people, including children and families. Those goals are important and worthy.
However, the mechanism and timing proposed in this amendment raise legitimate concerns.
This amendment does not merely preserve funding. It hardwires funding guarantees into statute, requiring the State Controller to ensure a minimum annual allocation of $65 million beginning in FY 2028 and permanently diverting up to 20% of cigarette and tobacco tax revenue to the Fund for a Healthy Maine. That represents a significant policy shift and a long-term commitment that reduces flexibility for future legislatures.
What is particularly troubling is the timing. At a moment when the public is grappling with recent revelations of large-scale fraud and abuse in publicly funded health and social service systems, including Medicaid and MaineCare-funded child care programs in other states, public confidence in oversight and accountability has been shaken. In that context, moving forward with mandatory funding floors and permanent revenue reallocations without first addressing oversight gaps sends the wrong message.
This is not an argument against public health funding. It is an argument for sequencing and safeguards. Before locking in guaranteed funding levels, the Legislature should be asking hard questions about auditing practices, internal controls, verification mechanisms, and enforcement capacity. Transparency and accountability should precede expansion and entrenchment of funding structures, not follow them.
I am also concerned that this amendment shifts the conversation from outcomes to assurances. Mandated funding levels do not, by themselves, guarantee effectiveness, efficiency, or integrity. Without strong, enforceable oversight, even well-intentioned funds can be misused or fail to deliver promised results.
For these reasons, I urge the Committee to pause and reconsider this approach. Strengthening public health requires not only sustained investment, but also demonstrable accountability, rigorous oversight, and public confidence that funds are being managed responsibly. Those elements should be addressed explicitly before permanent funding guarantees are enacted.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
Respectfully submitted, Colleen Wright Brown

My name is Jessica Fay and I am the Policy and Advocacy Director for the Maine Council on Aging (MCOA). The MCOA is a broad, multidisciplinary network of over 140 organizations, businesses, municipalities, and older community members working to ensure we can all live healthy, engaged, and secure lives with choices and opportunities as we age at home and in our communities.
I am testifying in support of LD 1658 "An Act to Preserve and Strengthen the Fund for a Healthy Maine".
Assuring the solvency of the Fund for Healthy Maine is critical for the health and well-being of many Maine people. The fund was created using tobacco settlement money and the mechanism proposed by Rep. Graham in LD 1658 makes sense given the purpose of both FHM and of the approved uses of the settlement funds.
The Fund for a Healthy Maine is an important source of funding for Maine's Low-Cost Drugs for the Elderly and Disabled (also known as "DEL"), The allocation of $6 million per year allows many low-income older Mainers (age 62 and older) to afford their prescription medications. For eligible people, DEL will pay the cost of 80% of certain prescriptions after a small co-pay and in some cases can also help cover the cost of Medicare Part D co-payment.
Given the increases in the cost of many prescriptions and the changes in availability of Medicare plans, DEL can be a lifeline for those who might need to choose between affording their medication and other necessities. We support the efforts to make the Fund for a Healthy Maine solvent for the future so that this benefit remains intact.
Thank you for the opportunity to submit these comments in support of LD 1658.

My name is Liz Blackwell-Moore, and I am the Director of Cumberland County Public Health. I'm here to speak in strong support of LD 1658, An Act to Preserve and Strengthen the Fund for a Healthy Maine.
At its core, LD 1658 is a prevention bill. It aligns our policies and our funding with what we know works in public health: stable funding, strategic investment, and upstream action that keeps people healthy long before they show up in emergency rooms, clinics, or treatment programs.
The Fund for a Healthy Maine was created with that exact vision in mind. Using tobacco settlement dollars to prevent disease, reduce tobacco use, support children and families, and strengthen community health was one of Maine's greatest public health achievements. But over time, as demands have grown and revenue streams have shifted, FHM is at risk which means prevention and public health are at risk of being under or unfunded.
LD 1658 restores that original promise by ensuring the Fund for a Healthy Maine has the resources in place each year to make baseline investments in public health and prevention. This is not an abstract calculation--it reflects the actual scale of prevention work that Maine communities require: tobacco cessation programs, early childhood supports, substance use prevention, preventative oral healthcare, chronic disease programming, and school- and community-based initiatives that reach people where they live, work, and learn. It also accounts for the current reality which is that we can't count on federal funding to meet the public health and prevention needs that we have in Maine.
I have spent the last 25 years working in public health, much of that time in substance use prevention. Over the past 7 or 8 years, I have seen a dramatic increase in the number of people in the community who talk about the importance of prevention. Even when the topic is treatment or recovery, the conversation ends up on prevention and how we must do more of it. There is some amazing prevention work happening, but it must continue to be funded!
This bill recognizes that prevention is not a cost--it is an investment. The US CDC estimates that for every dollar spent on comprehensive tobacco control programs, states get a $55 return on investment, mostly in averted health care costs to treat smoking-related illness. For every young person who doesn't use substances at an early age, for every adult who gets support to quit smoking, for every family who has access to resources that reduce future chronic disease, Maine becomes a healthier, stronger, and more financially stable state.
As a public health professional, I can tell you with certainty: we cannot build a healthy future on unstable or insufficient funding. LD 1658 gives Maine the tools to sustain prevention, support communities, and reduce the burden of disease for generations to come.
I urge you to support LD 1658 and help preserve and strengthen the Fund for a Healthy Maine. Thank you for your time and for your commitment to the health of our state.

Testimony of Maine Public Health Association in Support of: LD 1658: An Act to Preserve and Strengthen the Fund for a Healthy Maine
Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services Room 209, Cross Building Wednesday, January 7, 2026
Good afternoon, Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services. My name is Rebecca Boulos. I am the executive director of Maine Public Health Association. MPHA is in support of LD 1658: "An Act to Preserve and Strengthen the Fund for a Healthy Maine," as amended.
MPHA is the state's oldest, largest, and most diverse association for public health professionals. We represent nearly 950 individual and 80 organizational members across the state, and our mission is to advance the health of all people and places in Maine.
We strongly support an annual transfer of a portion of the state's tobacco excise tax into the Fund for a Healthy Maine (FHM).
Tobacco use is the leading cause of preventable cancer diagnoses and cancer deaths in the United States. According to our recently released toolkit, "Reducing Maine's Cancer Burden," increasing the tax on tobacco products is an evidence-based strategy for decreasing youth and adult smoking rates. In fact, every 10% increase in the real price of cigarettes is associated with a 6-10% decrease in youth smoking. 1 That's why we were grateful to the legislature for its leadership last session in increasing the Maine's tobacco tax for the first time in 20 years. And, because Maine passed tobacco tax equalization, emerging products - like electronic cigarettes and nicotine pouches that are popular among youth - will also see an equivalent tax increase.
Tax increases on tobacco products are successful because they increase the product price, which makes them more cost prohibitive to youth. Tax increases are also successful when paired with investments in tobacco prevention and treatment programming. Indeed, a 2021 analysis found that, "tobacco tax increases are less likely to be regressive when accompanied by a broad framework of demand-side measures that enhance the capacity of low-income smokers to quit tobacco use."2 Allocating a portion of the tax to the FHM will align the tax with its purpose - supporting the health of people in Maine, and giving smokers the resources and help they need to quit.
Further, the FHM faces a structural deficit. The original Master Settlement Agreement was based on the health harms of combustible cigarettes - e-cigarettes and nicotine pouches were not on the market then and so aren't included in the Settlement Agreement. That means that as fewer people smoke combustible cigarettes and more switch to nicotine alternatives, Maine is receiving fewer MSA funds, causing a structural deficit. The FHM houses several programs that support the health of people in Maine, including the state's tobacco prevention and treatment programs, school-based health centers, and other substance use prevention programs. With this annual transfer, we can make the FHM "whole" and ensure consistent funding for these critical public health programs.
Every year in Maine, the tobacco industry spends $45 million on product marketing, and 2,400 people die prematurely from smoking-related illnesses. We also pay $942 million in direct health care costs associated with tobacco use each year. We support LD 1658 because we should align the purpose of the tobacco tax with

Secure the Fund for a Healthy Maine for the Future
For 25 years, Maine people have protected their investment in the Fund for a Healthy Maine (FHM), the state's repository for payments from the 1998 Master Settlement Agreement. The state has been a national leader in aligning the purpose of this funding with its uses, investing in youth tobacco use prevention, addiction treatment, and access to health services and care.
The FHM has been approaching a financial crossroads for several years, caused by declining payments from the settlement, which are based on national cigarette sales and do not include nicotine pouches and vaping products. The 2027 fiscal year marks the exhaustion of the FHM carryover funds that have been masking its looming structural deficit, which could mean cuts to programming if nothing is changed.
In the continuing services budget passed in March 2025, Maine lawmakers stepped up to protect the FHM in the current biennium. Taking this action in such a challenging environment is much appreciated by Maine's public health professionals and acknowledges the value of prevention for Maine people and communities. But this was a one-time solution for an ongoing problem, so the future of the Fund remains uncertain.
We are in a moment of opportunity. We can take one final step to assure the Fund and its critical public health and prevention programs are financially stable and secure in the years ahead.
There is a straightforward solution that aligns tobacco-related revenue with tobacco-related expenses.
We, the undersigned public health professionals, support the transfer of a portion of tobacco excise tax revenue from the General Fund to the FHM as an annual and ongoing solution to the structural deficit in the Fund.
Maine should be proud of our FHM legacy. We have consistently used the FHM to support the health of youth and communities across the state. We can and must protect Maine's only dedicated source of funding for tobacco prevention and public health by securing the FHM for future generations.
We urge the Maine Legislature to pass LD 1658 and secure the future of the Fund for a Healthy Maine.

Testimony in Support of LD 1772 and LD 1658
Senator Inwersen, Representative Meyer, and honorable members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Health and Human Services,
My name is Renee Page, Executive Director at Healthy Communities of the Capital Area (HCCA), a public health primary prevention organization in Hallowell. I am testifying in favor of
LDs 1772 and 1658, which will strengthen and solidify Maine's public health efforts.
Maine has an almost 30-year history of successfully leveraging Master Tobacco Settlement dollars through the Fund fora Healthy Maine. These funds are used to implement primary prevention strategies to address costly and deleterious effects of chronic disease and addiction through a statewide network of local co1n1nunity--based public health organizations and other partners. This structure and the Fund have been threatened by proposed shifts, cuts, and restructuring time and time again often resulting in disruptions in services, efforts, and results.
The missing link is what LD 1772 proposes.
This bill establishes the Maine Commission on Public Health and Prevention to assist and advise the Legislature on evidence-based public health policies that will in turn solidify processes and plans for Maine's public health future to ensure public health needs are met, emerging threats are addressed, and outcomes achieved. This is an exciting opportunity for Maine to implement a Commission to provide the ongoing stability and guidance needed to prioritize public health issues and address them.
Public health primary prevention strategies supported by the Fund for a Healthy Maine are needed more than ever. Though Maine has a successful track record of reducing cigarette use and stemming the tide of opioid addiction, there is still a lot of work to be done to address emerging threats like vaping and other chronic disease indicators like poor diet, lack of physical activity, isolation, and more. To successfully mitigate these drivers of disease and addiction, Maine must have a solid, consistent implementation plan and the funding to support it. Healthcare costs continue to skyrocket, and more Mainers are losing access to healthcare coverage and healthcare facilities. The best way to lessen this burden is to help people get and remain healthy for as long as possible, which is what public health primary prevention does.
LD 1772 will support implementation of a well thought out plan that includes public health professionals, the Legislature, and Maine CDC to ensure less disruption of progress and secure
funding into the future.
LD 1658 goes a step further to solidify a state funding stream for tobacco prevention and
treatment efforts. This helps close the gap from decreasing Master Tobacco Settlement payments over time and only makes sense that some of the revenue from a tobacco tax would support prevention and treatment.
I respectfully request you to vote in favor of LD 1772 and LD 1658 to help solidify Maine's public
health infrastructure. Thank you.

Testimony of Maine Area Health Education Center (AHEC) Network at the University of New England Before the Committee on Health and Human Services January 7, 2026
LD 1658, An Act to Preserve and Strengthen the Fund for a Healthy Maine
Senator Graham and distinguished members of the Committee on Health and Human Services. My name is Zoe Hull. I am a resident of Westbrook and am the director of the Maine Area Health Education Center (AHEC) Network at the University of New England. I appreciate the opportunity to provide testimony today in support of the transfer of a portion of tobacco excise tax revenue from the General Fund to the Fund for a Healthy Maine as an annual and ongoing solution to the structural deficit in the Fund.
The Fund for a Healthy Maine currently provides critical funding for Maine AHEC Network, referred to in the state budget as the Health Education Centers, to develop and deliver healthcare workforce development programs in Maine. With declining payments from the 1998 Master Settlement Agreement, this work is put at risk. However, the transfer of a portion of tobacco excise tax revenue to the Fund for a Healthy Maine can ensure that healthcare workforce development efforts in the state remain funded and robust.
Established in 1994, Maine AHEC Network is a statewide healthcare workforce development program. We have four Health Education Centers with service areas that cover the whole state, including the University of New England which serves Southern Maine and also administers funding for the other Health Education Centers (Western: Franklin Memorial Hospital; Eastern: Healthy Acadia; Northern: Eastern Maine Medical Center). Our mission is to prepare and support Maine's healthcare workforce by creating healthcare learning opportunities for youth, students, and professionals to foster healthier communities and expand access to care across Maine. We fulfill our mission by:
� Encouraging and supporting Maine youth to pursue careers in the health professions � Delivering didactic and community-based education to health professions students to prepare them to
provide care for rural and medically underserved communities in Maine � Offering continuing education programs to practicing health professionals
Our programming is designed to address the healthcare workforce shortages in our state. All but one of Maine's counties are designated as having health professional shortage areas in at least one of the following domains: primary care, mental health, and dental health. The financial support provided by the Fund for a Healthy Maine makes it possible for Maine AHEC Network to deliver comprehensive healthcare workforce development programming to ensure the healthcare workforce is prepared to meet the needs of our communities.
The primary source of funding for Maine AHEC Network is the federal AHEC grant from the Health Resources and Services Administration. The AHEC grant requires a one to one match in funding. Because the annual match is quite large, we combine several sources of funds, and our funding from the Fund for a Healthy Maine is an important component of these matching funds. Without ongoing funding from this state fund, the federal funding coming into Maine that supports healthcare workforce development efforts could be jeopardized.
The use of a portion of tobacco excise tax revenue from the General Fund to the Fund for a Healthy Maine not only supports public health prevention work, it also supports healthcare workforce development efforts. We request that the Maine Legislature pass LD 1658 to ensure ongoing funding for essential healthcare workforce development that is needed to support the health of Maine people.
